episodes.title: Contract WS01 · Contract formation
recap: Shop displays and ordinary adverts are invitations to treat, so the customer makes the offer; only a unilateral advert, like a reward, is an offer.
A reply that changes the terms is a counter-offer and destroys the offer; a mere question leaves it open.
A posted acceptance takes effect on posting, unless the offer requires actual receipt, post is unreasonable or the letter is misaddressed; a revocation takes effect only on receipt.

An offer can be revoked any time before acceptance, even if promised open, unless the offeree gave consideration or has started to perform a unilateral offer; the performer must have known of the offer, and motive does not matter.
A vague key term, or an essential term left to be agreed with no machinery, means no contract; a meaningless subsidiary term is severed, and silence on price gets a reasonable price.
A lock-out binds only if it is for a definite period and supported by consideration; a promise to negotiate in good faith is unenforceable.

episodes.title: DR WS06 · Disclosure and privilege
recap: An adverse document must always be listed. Harm to your own case is never a ground to withhold, and privilege or disproportionality can stop only inspection.

Intermediate and multi-track claims without personal injury get a disclosure report, then the menu. Fast track and personal injury claims get whatever the court directs, for example standard disclosure.
Never listed means specific disclosure. Listed but inspection refused as disproportionate means specific inspection.
Pre-action and non-party disclosure: the respondent generally gets its costs of the application and of complying, even though it loses.
